extra.message: User-supplied 'name' and 'password' request parameters are concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to Statement.executeQuery(). An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. name=' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication or exfiltrate the 'secret' column for all users.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: The 'pingurl' request parameter is used, with no validation or allowlist, as the target URL for a server-side HttpURLConnection request. An unauthenticated attacker can make the server issue arbitrary GET requests to internal hosts/ports (e.g. pingurl=http://169.254.169.254/ or http://internal-host:port/) and observe response codes/timing, enabling SSRF-based internal network scanning and metadata access.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: User-controlled 'jsonString' is concatenated directly into a JavaScript string passed to ScriptEngine.eval(). Since Nashorn scripts can access arbitrary Java classes, breaking out of the quoted string (e.g. with a single quote) allows arbitrary JavaScript/Java code execution, leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The 'expression' request parameter is parsed and evaluated directly via Ognl.parseExpression/Ognl.getValue with no sandboxing beyond a trivial 'Math.' string replace. OGNL expressions can invoke static methods (e.g. @java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(...)), allowing arbitrary command execution via expression injection.

cwe: CWE-917: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement

extra.message: The 'uid' and 'password' POST parameters are concatenated unescaped into an LDAP filter string passed to FilterParser.parse(). An attacker can inject LDAP filter syntax (e.g. uid=*)(uid=*) to bypass authentication, unlike the sibling DefaultLoginServlet.authUser() which calls encodeForLDAP() on the same inputs.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: Uploaded files are written under the application's webapp directory (SAVE_DIR = 'uploadFiles', resolved via getRealPath) with no validation of file extension or content type. An attacker can upload a .jsp file, which the servlet container will execute if later requested directly, leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: For the '/xxe' path, the SAXParserFactory only sets FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true and does not disable external general/parameter entities or external DTD loading. An uploaded XML file with a SYSTEM entity (e.g. <!ENTITY % p1 SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">) will be resolved by the parser, allowing arbitrary local file disclosure, matching the attack documented in this servlet's own help text.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: For the '/xee' path, only external-general-entities and external DTD loading are disabled; internal entity expansion is not limited (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is not set on this branch). An uploaded XML file with nested internal ENTITY definitions (billion-laughs style, as shown in this servlet's own help text) causes exponential entity expansion and resource exhaustion.

cwe: CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')

extra.message: The uploaded file name is taken verbatim from the Content-Disposition header via MultiPartFileUtils.getFileName() and used directly in 'new File(fileName)' with no canonicalization or path-traversal check. An attacker can supply a filename like '../../../../tmp/evil.txt' or an absolute path to write the uploaded content to an arbitrary filesystem location.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The 'subject' value, sourced unsanitized from the 'subject' request parameter in MailHeaderInjectionServlet.doPost() (line 88-101), is passed directly to MimeMessage.setSubject() with no CRLF stripping. An attacker can embed CR/LF sequences in the subject to inject additional mail headers (e.g. Bcc:) or alter message structure.

cwe: CWE-93: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

extra.message: The 'string' request parameter is reversed and appended directly into the HTML response body without calling encodeForHTML(), unlike other servlets in this codebase. An attacker-supplied value like '<script>alert(1)</script>' is reflected unescaped, resulting in reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The 'goto' request parameter is passed directly to res.sendRedirect() after successful login with no validation that it is a same-origin/relative URL. An attacker can craft a login link with goto=https://evil.example.com to redirect authenticated users to an external phishing site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: doPost() changes the logged-in user's LDAP password based solely on the session 'userid' attribute and the submitted 'password' field, with no CSRF token generated in doGet()/validated in doPost(). A forged cross-site POST from an authenticated admin's browser can change their password without consent.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

extra.message: The X-FRAME-OPTIONS: DENY header is explicitly skipped for any request path starting with '/admins/clickjacking'. This endpoint (ClickJackingServlet) renders a form that changes the logged-in user's e-mail address, so omitting frame protection allows the page to be embedded in an attacker's iframe for a clickjacking attack.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: doPost() calls authUser(userid, password) directly with no call to isAccountLocked()/incrementLoginFailedCount(), unlike the parent DefaultLoginServlet and sibling VerboseErrorMessageServlet. This allows unlimited login attempts against the LDAP backend with no rate limiting or lockout, enabling password brute-forcing.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: On successful authentication, the existing HTTP session (obtained via req.getSession(true), which returns any pre-existing session) is reused and simply marked 'authenticated'; the session ID is never regenerated/invalidated-and-recreated. Reached via '/sessionfixation/login' (SessionFixationServlet, which inherits this doPost unchanged), an attacker can fixate a victim's session ID before login and gain access post-authentication.

cwe: CWE-384: Session Fixation

extra.message: doPost() returns distinct messages for 'account locked', 'user not exist', 'password format invalid', and 'password not match', instead of a single generic authentication failure message. This observable discrepancy lets an attacker enumerate valid usernames and learn the account-lockout threshold.

cwe: CWE-203: Observable Discrepancy
CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The '/exit' endpoint is not covered by AuthenticationFilter (only paths starting with '/admins' require auth) and calls System.exit(0) on any GET request, immediately terminating the entire JVM/application for all users with no authentication required.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The '/infiniteloop' endpoint requires no authentication and enters an unconditional 'while(true)' loop that never returns, permanently occupying a request-handling thread per call. A handful of concurrent requests exhausts the servlet container's thread pool, causing denial of service for the whole application.

cwe: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

extra.message: selectUsers() acquires a JDBC Connection/Statement/ResultSet but the finally block that would close them is commented out (lines 84-89). Every unauthenticated request to '/dbconnectionleak' leaks a database connection, eventually exhausting the connection pool/driver resources and causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The unauthenticated '/filedescriptorleak' endpoint opens a FileOutputStream/OutputStreamWriter and a BufferedReader/FileReader on every request and never closes any of them. Repeated requests leak file descriptors until the process hits its OS file-handle limit, causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: Every unauthenticated request to '/threadleak' starts a new ThreadCountLoggingThread that loops forever (while(true) { sleep(100000); ... }) and is never stopped or tracked. Repeated requests accumulate live threads indefinitely, exhausting OS/JVM thread resources and causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: toDoRemove() appends a unique ~1.9MB string into the servlet-instance field 'cache' (a HashMap that is never cleared) on every unauthenticated request to '/memoryleak'. Repeated requests grow heap usage without bound, eventually triggering OutOfMemoryError and denial of service.

cwe: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

extra.message: The user-supplied 'word' parameter is matched against the pattern '^([a-z0-9]+[-]{0,1}){1,100}$', which exhibits catastrophic backtracking on crafted input (e.g. a long run of digits/letters followed by a non-matching character). A single unauthenticated request can pin a worker thread at 100% CPU for an extended period, enabling a ReDoS-based denial of service.

cwe: CWE-1333: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: @MultipartConfig is declared with no arguments, leaving maxFileSize and maxRequestSize at their unlimited (-1) defaults. The '/ursupload' endpoint accepts uploads of unbounded size with no server-side cap, allowing an attacker to exhaust disk space or memory via oversized uploads.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The 'fileName' request parameter is concatenated with '.pdf' and used directly to build a File path under the 'pdf' directory, with no sanitization of path-traversal sequences ('../'). While the forced '.pdf' suffix limits exposure on current JVMs, directory-traversal sequences combined with any file ending in '.pdf' elsewhere on disk can still be reached and streamed back to the client via this download endpoint.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Plaintext admin and user passwords (e.g. 'password', 'pas2w0rd', 'pa33word') are hardcoded in source and inserted into the 'users' table at application startup, disclosing these credentials to anyone who reads the source.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: Plaintext admin passwords ('password', 'pas2w0rd', 'pa33word', 'pathwood') are hardcoded in source and loaded directly into the embedded LDAP directory at startup, disclosing these credentials to anyone who reads the source.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
